spatial_claims.claim: AB and CD are parallel straight lines; E is a point on AB; F is a point on CD
AB and CD lie in the same plane P (by definition of parallel lines, D1.23)
E lies in plane P (since E is on AB and AB is in P)
F lies in plane P (since F is on CD and CD is in P)
Both endpoints E and F of line EF are in plane P
If any part of EF were not in P, part would be in P and part elevated, contradicting 11.1
The whole straight line EF lies in plane P

configuration_map: Plane P is the plane containing parallel lines AB and CD (guaranteed by the definition of parallel lines). Point E is on line AB, hence in plane P. Point F is on line CD, hence in plane P. Line EF joins E to F with both endpoints in plane P. By 11.1, the entire line EF must lie in plane P. All objects (AB, CD, E, F, EF) are coplanar in P. No auxiliary constructions, no interior/exterior point claims, no angle decompositions.
pass_reason: All spatial claims in the proof concern plane membership and are mutually consistent. The chain of reasoning (parallel lines share a plane P; points on those lines are in P; a line with both endpoints in P lies entirely in P by 11.1) involves no contradictory geometric configurations. There are no angle decompositions, interior/exterior point arguments, or complex constructions that could introduce inconsistency.
